title: The dispatch suites assert written counts of the tree's utilities and arms, so a new utility means editing them
body:
`opt/utilz/test/help_dispatch.bats` and `opt/utilz/test/version_dispatch.bats` check every sweep of the tree's utilities against a written count of them, and `help_dispatch.bats` checks the utilities that own a `--help` arm, and the renderer arms in `show_help`, against written counts too. hv's rule: no count goes into a test, and a count already written down is deleted, never corrected. Each new utility turns these rows red until the numbers are edited, which is why `intent/restart.md` lists "the arm count in `help_dispatch.bats`" among the rosters a new utility bumps.

## What

Line numbers are at `55d68f7e`.

- `help_dispatch.bats:22` and `version_dispatch.bats:27` set `_expected_count` to the number of utilities the tree holds today, and every sweeping row compares its own count with it (`help_dispatch.bats:32`, `:46`, `:66`, `:85`, `:101` and `:201`; `version_dispatch.bats:32`, `:47`, `:60` and `:74`). Failing loudly on a narrowed glob ("the glob is wrong, not the tree") is the right control; the written number is what is wrong with it.
- `help_dispatch.bats:202` compares the utilities that carry their own `--help` arm with a written count, though `:203` already names prez as the utility that delegates, so the count adds nothing the name does not.
- `help_dispatch.bats:135` asks for at least a written number of renderer arms in `show_help`, while its message names them (glow, bat).
- The suites define `_utilities` identically, at `help_dispatch.bats:12` and `version_dispatch.bats:17`, so the population they sweep has a home in each file instead of one.

## Found

cc, planning issue 0113 on 27 Oct 2026: these are counts in test code, outside 0113's test names and comments.

## Design

- The population has one home: `_utilities` moves to `opt/utilz/test/test_helper.bash`, with the reader of the link set beside it (vc), and the dispatch suites read both there.
- A narrowed sweep still fails loudly, against a set read independently of the glob instead of a number: the names of the links in `$UTILZ_BIN_DIR` that point at `utilz`. A row in each suite asserts that `_utilities` names exactly that set, and that the set is not empty; on a difference it names each name on either side and says the glob is wrong, not the tree. Each sweeping row compares its own count with that set's size, read at the run.
- `help_dispatch.bats:202` is deleted: `:203` names prez as the utility that delegates, and the population row names the set, so every other swept utility carries its arm with no number.
- The renderer row names the renderers it expects, glow and bat, and finds each one's invocation in `show_help`; the check that every invocation it finds closes stdin stays.
- The comments on the lines this changes are reworded with them; the other comments in these files are 0113's, which sweeps them after this lands.
- `intent/restart.md` drops "the arm count in `help_dispatch.bats`" from its rosters on the landing (vc's file).
- Proof by mutation, one at a time, each restored: the glob in `_utilities` narrowed (`opt/*/` to `opt/[a-m]*/`) turns the population rows and every sweeping row red; the link set's reader narrowed the same way turns the population rows red, and the sweeping rows with them; a renderer's invocation removed from `show_help` in the worktree turns the renderer row red; and one utility's `-h | --help)` arm renamed in the worktree (todo's) turns the arm row red through `:203`, which proves that deleting `:202` loses nothing (vc).

## Scope

For the release after 2.14.4, stacked with 0113. vc read the design on 27 Oct and approved it, adding the arm mutation, and checked that the opt glob's set and bin's links to utilz name the same utilities today. cc's, in a worktree under `~/Devel/scratch/utilz-cc/`. Every bats suite loads `test_helper.bash`, so the runs, booked through vc, are every bats suite (`bats opt/*/test`) under bash 3.2 and bash 5, then dc's kovacs leg on the same bytes. It lands by path on vc's word, after 0116 and before 0113 sweeps these files; its landing is 0113's base commit, so its green runs serve as 0113's suite base (vc). Size S.
